Every project has an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server (`<game>_mcp` from the checkout build, or
the stock `mce_mcp --module <lib<game>.so>`, `mce mcp` with the SDK) that gives an AI agent
the same scene-editing commands a person has in the editor, plus cook and headless verification.
Three games in the repository were authored entirely this way (Kindle's level, Prism Break and
Undertow), and a fourth (Lamplighter) by an agent that had never seen the engine source. This
chapter is the workflow that worked and the pitfalls it found.

# 9. Physics

2D physics is scene-authored: a body is an entity with `RigidBody2D` and `Collider2D`, the engine
steps the world every fixed tick in `FixedUpdate_Physics` and writes the resulting poses into
`LocalTransform`. Game code reads events and controller state, moves kinematic bodies by velocity,
and uses queries. 3D physics is the kit's `Physics3D` world with static `BoxCollider3D` / `MeshCollider3D` (sections 8.2 and 8.7).

## 9.1 Bodies and colliders

```json
"Ground": {
  "LocalTransform": { "position": [0, -3, 0] },
  "RigidBody2D": {},
  "Collider2D": { "shape": { "half": [10, 0.5] }, "density": 0 }
},
"Crate": {
  "LocalTransform": { "position": [0, 5, 0] },
  "RigidBody2D": { "type": "Dynamic" },
  "Collider2D": {}
}
```

`RigidBody2D`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | `Static` (never moves), `Kinematic` (moved by you, pushes others), `Dynamic` (simulated) |
| `fixed_rotation` | keep the body upright |
| `layer` | this body's collision layer, 0..15 |
| `mask` | bit set of layers it collides with (`0xFFFF` = all; a sensor that should see only layer 1 has `mask: 2`) |
| `gravity_scale` | 0 for characters and floating things |
| `linear_damping` | velocity decay |

`Collider2D`: one shape per body plus `density` (0 = massless, which static and kinematic bodies
should use), `friction`, `restitution`, `is_sensor` (overlap events, no collision response),
`one_way` (blocks the character controller only when it moves downward: platforms you jump through).

# 8. 3D games

A 3D game is a scene of **kit3d components** plus a game module, played by the stock player, the
same way a 2D game is a scene of 2D kit components (chapter 7). The scene places models, lights, a
camera, the sky and static colliders; the module's systems move things and drive the camera; the
player draws it all with the physically based forward renderer (cascaded shadows, Forward+ point
and spot lights, sky, fog, bloom, tonemap, FXAA) and runs it headless, with `-capture_tick`,
`-input` scripts and `-save` slots like any other game. The editor viewport shows the same scene.

`projects/Room3D` is the small reference (`mce example Room3D` copies it out of the SDK) and
`projects/SolsticeReach` the large one: an island with a time of day, scatter, beams and a HUD,
all from a module on the kit. A program that owns its renderer (`samples/04_cubes`,
`05_ashen_court`) still works and is covered at the end of the chapter.

# 11. Input

Gameplay never sees keys, buttons or SDL events. Each fixed tick the engine folds every device
event into one immutable snapshot, `input::InputState`, and your systems read that. The snapshot
is part of the determinism contract: it can be recorded and replayed, and the same snapshot
sequence gives the same game.

## 11.1 Reading input

```cpp
void player(Frame& f) {
    const input::InputState& in = f.resource<input::InputState>();
    const f32 mx = in.move.x;                 // -1..1, WASD / arrows / left stick / d-pad
    if (in.jump_pressed) { ... }              // edge: this tick only
    if (in.jump_held) { ... }                 // level
    if (in.fire_pressed) { ... }
    if (in.pause_pressed) { ... }
    const bool dash = in.has_action(MCE_SID("Dash")) ? in.pressed(MCE_SID("Dash")) : in.fire_pressed;
}
```

| Member | Action | Default bindings |
|---|---|---|
| `move` (vec2) | Move | W A S D, arrows, left stick, d-pad |
| `look` (vec2) | Look | mouse delta, right stick |
| `jump_pressed` / `jump_held` / `jump_released` | Jump | Space, gamepad South (A) |
| `fire_pressed` | Fire | J, left mouse, gamepad West (X) |
| `pause_pressed` | Pause | Escape, Start |
| `confirm_pressed`, `cancel_pressed` | Confirm, Cancel (UI map) | Enter or Space, Escape; South, East |
| `text()` | typed text this tick (UTF-8) | |
| `mouse_pos_px()`, `mouse_wheel()` | pointer state at the tick's end | |
